title: Atlas · Wed Nov 18 · 2:30pm
big_picture: Taylor, Nvidia's report did not hold the chip trade up. NVDA opened about 4% higher on the beat, then reversed and closed at 150.96 (-2.9%) on twice its usual volume, its lowest close since June 2025 ([TECHi](https://www.techi.com/nvidia-stock-falls-day-after-earnings-ten-report-record/), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/stock-market-today-live-updates.html)). Micron closed 705.27 (-1.0%) and the chip ETF SMH was flat (-0.1%), so the group did not break down; it just refused to rally. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell 0.3%, its fifth down day in a row; 48% of large caps are above their 50-day. The Fed minutes read hawkish: nearly everyone saw further rate rises as likely, markets price a December hike at roughly 95%, and the 10-year yield is near 5.1% ([Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-11-18/gold-prices-remain-under-pressure-fed-minutes-show-central-bank-committed), [Discovery Alert](https://discoveryalert.com/news/gold-price-below-3800-fed-hike-november-2026/)). Anthropic is reported to have priced its IPO at $83, above the $70-78 range, and starts trading Thursday as ANT ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-18/anthropic-is-said-to-price-ipo-at-83-per-share)). That price comes from people familiar with the matter, so I treat it as reported, not confirmed, until the company announces it.

sectors.numbers: chips fell 31.1% from the high, 8.3% off the low, 10% up 2%+ today; communication equipment fell 28.4%, 5.7% off the low, 39% up 2%+; hardware fell 33.8%, at its low, 17% up 2%+
sectors.why: the group's low is still its Nov 5 low, and today's premarket gain faded by the close. Two things in Nvidia's report are not clean: receivables of $81.0B up 29% while revenue rose 20% (about 64 days of sales, the most since 2022), and $118B of guarantees that Nvidia says take effect only as buildings finish and have had no payments so far ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nvidia-interim-ceo-guarantee-doesn-153404226.html), [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/17/nvidia-has-a-usd118-billion-promise-tucked-inside-its-blowout-quarter-here-s-what-it-means-for-the-stock/)). The 10-Q is not filed yet, so the make-up of both comes from the release and call. What would change the view: MU closing under $650, SMH under its Nov 5 low of 447.73 (it closed 459.54), or NVDA closing under today's 150.96.

sectors.why: cyber stocks rallied hard before Palo Alto's report, with Qualys, Tenable and Palo Alto up between 9.9% and 15.8% in the price files; one outlet ties the move to a DHS warning that hackers are using AI to scale attacks ([FourWeekMBA](https://fourweekmba.com/ai-cyber-stocks-jump-up-to-11-5-ahead-of-palo-altos-results/), [Business Upturn](https://businessupturn.com/usa/money/us-markets/top-movers-cyber-security-stocks-surge-while-miners-retreat-wednesday-18-november-2026/)). That reason is one outlet's, not confirmed by DHS in what I found. Palo Alto then reported after the close: revenue $3.45B against $3.31B expected, adjusted EPS $1.05 against $0.97, and an acquisition (Applied Compute); the stock was up about 8% after hours ([Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/26/11/63414200/palo-alto-posts-q1-double-beat-announces-applied-compute-acquisition)). MarketBeat shows a different EPS (a GAAP figure); I used the adjusted one. What would change the view: the group giving back the day on the open.

Reports say spot gold fell below $3,800 to a one-year low (about $3,720, down more than 3% in one report) on the hawkish minutes and 5% yields, with US miners down 2-4% early ([Kitco](https://www.kitco.com/news/article/2026-11-18/gold-prices-remain-under-pressure-fed-minutes-show-central-bank-committed), [MINING.COM](https://www.mining.com/web/gold-price-drops-to-14-month-low-as-dollar-yields-rise-on-hawkish-fed-rhetoric/)). The files show the Canadian miners flat to up (group +0.4%, OGC.TO +1.4%), likely because Canadian closes came before the late drop. Not reconciled; I would not read the group's stage as a bounce until the next close. What would change the view: gold reclaiming $3,850, or a new low in the miners.

notes: Your lesson L6 (perception over numbers) fits here: Nvidia beat, guided about $130B for next quarter against roughly $125B expected, and the stock still fell. The numbers did not decide the day; the outlook and the guarantees did. One day only: the one-week read is still ahead.

Plan for tomorrow: nothing in chips or gold is an entry. Watch whether NVDA holds 150.96, MU holds 650, and how ANT trades (Micron is a buyer in the placement); wait 15-30 minutes after the 7:30am open before anything.

The $118B is $105B of SB Energy credit support, $9.5B power and systems, $3.5B land and shell; none paid, first one expected to take effect in fiscal 2029; receivables $81.0B ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/nvidia-interim-ceo-guarantee-doesn-153404226.html), [Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/17/nvidia-has-a-usd118-billion-promise-tucked-inside-its-blowout-quarter-here-s-what-it-means-for-the-stock/)). I read search summaries; the 10-Q is not out. Several pages would not open directly.

Trend board changes: AI build-out stays "fading". New evidence: NVDA reversed to its lowest close since June 2025 despite the beat; Anthropic's reported $83 price (a rumour until confirmed; the kill "prices below range" did not happen); receivables 64 days of sales; hawkish Fed minutes as a headwind. No kill has hit: MU is above $650 and SMH has no new low. Two new trends opened as "watching": Cyber and infrastructure software bounce, and Rate-hike pressure (gold, growth stocks).

Your lessons: L6 held on day one: NVDA beat and guided up, then closed -2.9% after reversing a +3.9% premarket gain, while SMH closed -0.1% and MU -1.0%, so the group was not crushed. Held 1, failed 0. The one-week move is still to come. L1 and L2 not tested.
